stem: After an LST adjustment, one shoot slows temporarily while neighboring shoots continue normally. What should determine whether another adjustment is made?
choices: Follow the planned daily adjustment schedule so all shoots receive comparable training even if one shoot is still recovering.
Observed recovery, tissue condition, and canopy response before adding more mechanical stress.
Use container color and surface temperature as the main cues because they are more consistent than short-term shoot growth differences.
Repeat the adjustment at the same time of day because matching timing is more important than the individual shoot response.
rationale: Recovery and plant response should guide the timing and intensity of subsequent training, not an arbitrary schedule.
